title: apikey session stitching lag during dedicated regional cutover causes intermittent 403s
creator: Asha Patel
environment: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Gateway Edge Proxies
description: During a scheduled dedicated region cutover (capacity rebalance), some customers observed intermittent 403/authorization failures for valid API keys. The failures surfaced as short-lived "unauthorized" errors (~1-3s windows) for production traffic and were concentrated on instances being drained and reattached to new routing tables.
impact_summary: Two enterprise Dedicated customers (reported: Nimbus Retail, AtlasPay) hit transient authorization failures affecting checkout/ingest pipelines. Errors were customer-visible and triggered support SLAs and a Pager duty escalation. No long-term token leakage detected, but user-facing failures for ~30 minutes during migration windows.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a Dedicated capacity cutover simulation: drain worker group A and reattach to worker group B behind regional edge proxies.
2) Issue a token refresh workflow (client rotates API key or session refresh) during the drain event.
3) Send back-to-back requests from the same client using the newly refreshed API key while proxy routing tables update.
4) Observe intermittent 403s for requests that arrive during the approx 500-1500ms propagation window to some backend worker nodes.
5) Repeating with increased concurrency amplifies rate of failures.
Notes: failures only reproduce when routing state and session cache propagate asynchronously between edge proxies and backend pool managers.

2026-03-10 09:20 UTC - On-call engineer confirmed intermittent 403s tied to API key auth path; elevated to eng owners.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Mitigation: temporarily extended graceful-drain TTL and enabled request-retention fallback on gateway (reduced error surface).
2026-03-10 13:40 UTC - Root-cause hypothesis formed: session metadata (session->org binding) was not atomically visible to routing layer during worker reattach.
2026-03-11 02:15 UTC - Dev cluster reproducer created and load-tested; failure windows matched production.

mitigation: Short-term: increased drain TTL on affected Dedicated pools and enabled proxy-side sticky fallback that prefers last-known-good session binding when auth verification is transient. This reduced customer errors to near zero while we implemented the fix.
root_cause: A race between token refresh propagation and the backend routing table update during worker reattachment. The session creation path updates the per-worker session cache asynchronously; during cutover the routing layer sometimes routed the new token to a worker whose session cache had not yet been populated, causing the auth layer to treat the token as unbound to the expected org and fail.
fix_details: Implemented an atomic session-seed handshake: when a refreshed token is issued we now write a short-lived session-seed entry into the routing metadata store (fast-path KV) and make routing decisions consult that seed for the first 2s after rotation. Additionally added idempotent session reconcile on worker attach to ensure session cache warmup completes before taking traffic. Code changes in runtime auth path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8274.
testing_plan: Reproducer runs in dev and staging with variable drain timings, concurrency, and regional proxy topologies. Added integration tests that assert zero 403s for 30s windows around simulated cutovers and unit tests for session-seed write/read semantics. Load tests run with same traffic profile as Nimbus Retail (40k rps mixed) to validate stability.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix to release branch (runtime-1.23), 2) Canary rollout to low-traffic Dedicated pools for 2h with synthetic test traffic and convergence metrics, 3) Gradual 20/40/100% expansion across Dedicated pools over 48h, 4) Post-rollout validation and rollback window of 6h.
